title: "GHG flux models: visit-level data with a site random effect"
subtitle: "CH4 and CO2, 48 sites x 2 visits, all-subsets selection with dredge"
date: today

## Purpose

`GHG_Dredge.qmd` averages the two visits at each site (n = 48). This notebook
keeps both visits (n = 96) and adds a random intercept for site:

    flux ~ site-level predictors + visit-level weather + (1 | Site_ID)

**Why the random effect.** The two visits at a site are not independent: the
site intercept absorbs whatever makes a site high or low that the predictors
don't explain. Without it, the 96 rows would be treated as 96 independent
sites and every standard error would be too small. With 48 sites (levels) the
site variance is estimable. With only 2 visits per site, random *slopes* are
not, so the model has a random intercept only.

**Weather split into a site part and a visit part.** Each visit-level weather
variable `v` (e.g. ERA5 14-day mean temperature) enters as two predictors:

* `v_site`: the mean of the two visits at the site. This is what
  `GHG_Dredge.qmd` uses. It describes when (season, year) and where the site
  was sampled, so it is confounded with everything else about the site.
* `v_dev`: the visit's difference from that mean (± half the change between
  rounds). It is exactly uncorrelated with every site-level predictor, and its
  coefficient is the **within-site** effect: was flux higher on the warmer
  visit at the same site? That effect is estimated from the 48 pairs alone.

For upscaling to a typical summer day, set `v_dev = 0` and `v_site` to a
reference value (Section 6).

### How dredge is handled with a random effect

* **Only the fixed effects are selected.** `(1 | Site_ID)` is in every model.
  Its need is tested once, on the null model (Section 2).
* **Fits use ML (`REML = FALSE`).** REML likelihoods of models with different
  fixed effects are not comparable, so AICc/BIC from REML fits must not be
  used to rank them.
* **AICc uses n = 96.** For site-level predictors the effective sample size
  is closer to 48, so AICc is slightly lenient toward them. `RANK = "BIC"` is
  stricter.
* **R²** is reported as marginal (fixed effects only) and conditional (fixed
  plus site intercept), from `MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM()`.
* **The permutation test keeps the pairing.** Shuffling single visits would
  break the site structure, so whole sites are shuffled (both visits move
  together) and the two visits within each site are swapped at random. That
  keeps the site variance in every shuffle and removes any link to the
  predictors.
* **Cross-validation holds out whole sites** (both visits) and predicts them
  from the fixed effects only (`re.form = NA`), because a new site has no
  estimated intercept. This is the upscaling situation.
* **Speed.** An `lmer` fit takes ~25× as long as an `lm` fit, so the defaults
  are smaller than in `GHG_Dredge.qmd` (`M_MAX = 4`, fewer permutations). The
  dredge chunk prints the number of models before fitting.

**Reading the output.** As in `GHG_Dredge.qmd`: use the permutation test and
cross-validation to decide whether there is a signal, and the summed weights
and top-model set to decide which predictors carry it. Coefficient intervals
don't account for the selection step.

## Settings

```{r settings}
## ============================================================================
## Candidate predictor pool
## ============================================================================
WINDOW <- 10 # raster window (m): 10, 30 or 50

## Raster bands and statistics; each band x stat becomes "<band>_<stat>"
RASTER_BANDS <- c("DEM", "twi", "HAND", "CHM", "TPI", "DMV",
                  "NDVI", "NDWI", "NDVI_lo", "NDWI_lo", "WETprob")
RASTER_STATS <- c("mean", "sd")

## Site-level climate (same for both visits): PRISM normals
SITE_CLIMATE_VARS <- c("prism_ppt_annual", "prism_tmean_annual")

## Visit-level weather from NYDEC_GHG_Site_Climate.csv. Short names:
## "temperature_2m" -> "tmean", "total_precipitation_sum" -> "ppt".
## "doy" (day of year of the visit) can be added here as well.
VISIT_VARS <- c("era5_temperature_2m_14d", "era5_total_precipitation_sum_14d")

## TRUE: each visit variable enters as <v>_site + <v>_dev (see Purpose).
## FALSE: the raw visit value, which mixes within- and between-site effects.
WEATHER_SPLIT <- TRUE

## Hand adjustments to the pool (short names, e.g. "DEM_sd", "era5_tmean_14d_dev")
EXCLUDE <- character() # never in the pool
PROTECT <- character() # always in the pool; the VIF screen won't drop these
FIXED <- character()   # in every model (dredge `fixed =`); also protected

## Interactions to offer dredge, e.g. c("WETprob_mean:era5_tmean_14d_dev").
## An interaction uses 3 of the M_MAX terms.
INTERACTIONS <- character()

## ============================================================================
## Pool screening
## ============================================================================
VIF_MAX <- 10  # drop highest-VIF predictor until all are below this; Inf = off
COR_MAX <- 0.7 # pairs with |Spearman rho| >= this can't share a model; 1 = off

## ============================================================================
## Dredge
## ============================================================================
M_MIN <- 0       # min fixed terms per model (0 = include the null model)
M_MAX <- 4       # max fixed terms per model (counts fixed terms and interactions)
RANK <- "AICc"   # "AICc", "AIC" or "BIC"
DELTA_TOP <- 2   # "top set" = models within this many units of the best

## ============================================================================
## Responses
## ============================================================================
CH4_TRANSFORM <- "log_shift" # "log_shift" = log(CH4 + c); "asinh" = asinh(CH4 / s)
SHIFT_ADD <- 0.02            # c = |min(CH4)| + SHIFT_ADD (min over the 96 visits)
ASINH_SCALE <- 0.02          # s

## ============================================================================
## Checks against selection on noise
## ============================================================================
N_PERM <- 50        # restricted permutations (0 = skip); each re-runs dredge
CV_SCHEME <- "site" # "site" (leave one site out), "spatial" (leave out sites
                    # within CV_BLOCK_KM of each other), "ecoregion", or "none"
CV_BLOCK_KM <- 25
CV_PREDICT <- "best" # "best" = top model of each fold; "average" = top-set average

N_CORES <- min(8, parallel::detectCores()) # 1 = serial
SEED <- 1

## ============================================================================
## Candidate formulas (Section 5): hand-picked fixed effects, checked one by one
## ============================================================================
## Named list of one-sided-response formulas WITHOUT the random effect; it is
## added automatically. Response: CH4_resp or CO2. list() skips Section 5.
CANDIDATES <- list(
  `CH4 WETprob + tmean` = CH4_resp ~ WETprob_mean*DMV_sd*era5_tmean_14d_site
)

## ============================================================================
## Upscaling reference (Section 6)
## ============================================================================
## Value of each <v>_site for the "typical summer day" prediction, in raw
## units (e.g. c(era5_tmean_14d_site = 21)). Unlisted ones use the median of
## the site means. <v>_dev is set to 0.
REF_WEATHER <- c()
```

```{r setup}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(here)
library(lme4)
library(MuMIn)
library(parallel)

options(na.action = "na.fail") # dredge requires this

RASTER_CSV <- here("Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_Site_RasterPredictors.csv")
CLIMATE_CSV <- here("Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_Site_Climate.csv")
SITES_GPKG <- here("Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_Sites_EcoEPA_6347.gpkg")

## Skipping the gradient check at convergence speeds up lmer ~30%. The fits
## are simple (one variance component), so convergence problems are rare.
LMER_CTRL <- lmerControl(calc.derivs = FALSE)

## nobars() moved from lme4 to reformulas; use whichever is installed
nobars <- if (requireNamespace("reformulas", quietly = TRUE)) reformulas::nobars else lme4::nobars

## SD of the site random intercept (0 for a singular fit)
sd_site <- function(m) as.data.frame(VarCorr(m))$sdcor[1]

RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG") # reproducible random streams across parallel workers
set.seed(SEED)

stopifnot(
  CH4_TRANSFORM %in% c("log_shift", "asinh"),
  CV_SCHEME %in% c("site", "spatial", "ecoregion", "none"),
  CV_PREDICT %in% c("best", "average"),
  RANK %in% c("AICc", "AIC", "BIC")
)

## --- Plot styling (same palette as the other GHG notebooks) -----------------
WT_COLS <- c(EM = "#2a78d6", FO = "#eb6834", SS = "#1baf7a")
WT_SHAPES <- c(EM = 16, FO = 17, SS = 15)
RESP_COLS <- c(CH4 = "#2a78d6", CO2 = "#eb6834")
LEVEL_COLS <- c(site = "#898781", visit = "#1baf7a")
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#e1e0d9", linewidth = 0.3),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
          plot.title.position = "plot",
          legend.position = "top")
)
```

## 1. Data

One row per visit. Site-level predictors repeat across a site's two visits.

```{r load}
short_clim <- function(x) {
  x |> sub("total_precipitation_sum", "ppt", x = _) |>
    sub("temperature_2m", "tmean", x = _)
}

raster_cols <- c(outer(RASTER_BANDS, RASTER_STATS, \(b, s) sprintf("%s_%s_%dm", b, s, WINDOW)))
raster_short <- sub(sprintf("_%dm$", WINDOW), "", raster_cols)

flux <- st_read(SITES_GPKG, quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(Site_ID, Site_ID_round, Round_Number, CH4 = CH4_avg, CO2 = CO2_avg)

clim <- read.csv(CLIMATE_CSV) |>
  mutate(doy = as.integer(format(as.Date(Date), "%j"))) |>
  select(Site_ID_round, Date, all_of(SITE_CLIMATE_VARS), all_of(VISIT_VARS)) |>
  rename_with(short_clim, -c(Site_ID_round, Date))
visit_short <- short_clim(VISIT_VARS)

dat <- flux |>
  left_join(clim, by = "Site_ID_round") |>
  left_join(read.csv(RASTER_CSV, colClasses = c(huc12 = "character")) |>
              select(Site_ID, Ecoregion, Wetland_Type, x, y, all_of(raster_cols)) |>
              rename_with(\(v) sub(sprintf("_%dm$", WINDOW), "", v)),
            by = "Site_ID") |>
  arrange(Site_ID, Round_Number) |>
  mutate(Site_ID = factor(Site_ID),
         Ecoregion = factor(Ecoregion),
         Wetland_Type = factor(Wetland_Type, levels = names(WT_COLS)))

## Within-site split of the visit-level weather
if (WEATHER_SPLIT) {
  for (v in visit_short) {
    dat[[paste0(v, "_site")]] <- ave(dat[[v]], dat$Site_ID)
    dat[[paste0(v, "_dev")]] <- dat[[v]] - dat[[paste0(v, "_site")]]
  }
  visit_preds <- c(paste0(visit_short, "_site"), paste0(visit_short, "_dev"))
} else {
  visit_preds <- visit_short
}

## Two visits per site, rounds 1 and 2 in adjacent rows (the restricted
## permutation in Section 4.1 relies on this order)
stopifnot(nrow(dat) == 96, nlevels(dat$Site_ID) == 48,
          all(dat$Round_Number == rep(1:2, 48)),
          all(dat$Site_ID[c(TRUE, FALSE)] == dat$Site_ID[c(FALSE, TRUE)]),
          !anyNA(dat))

## Response transforms
ch4_shift <- abs(min(dat$CH4)) + SHIFT_ADD
dat$CH4_resp <- switch(CH4_TRANSFORM,
  log_shift = log(dat$CH4 + ch4_shift),
  asinh = asinh(dat$CH4 / ASINH_SCALE)
)
RESPONSES <- c(CH4 = "CH4_resp", CO2 = "CO2")
RESP_LABELS <- c(CH4 = sprintf("CH4 (%s)", sub("_", " ", CH4_TRANSFORM)), CO2 = "CO2")

all_preds <- setdiff(c(raster_short, SITE_CLIMATE_VARS, visit_preds), EXCLUDE)
stopifnot(all(c(PROTECT, FIXED) %in% all_preds))
pred_level <- function(p) ifelse(grepl("_dev$", p) | p %in% visit_short, "visit", "site")
```

How much the weather changes between a site's visits, compared with the
spread between sites:

```{r weather-split}
if (WEATHER_SPLIT) {
  map_dfr(visit_short, \(v) tibble(
    variable = v,
    sd_between_sites = sd(dat[[paste0(v, "_site")]][c(TRUE, FALSE)]),
    sd_within_site = sd(dat[[paste0(v, "_dev")]]),
    round2_minus_round1_mean = mean(diff(matrix(dat[[v]], nrow = 2))),
    round2_minus_round1_range = paste(round(range(diff(matrix(dat[[v]], nrow = 2))), 2),
                                      collapse = " to ")
  )) |>
    kable(digits = 2, caption = "Visit-level weather: between-site vs within-site variation")
}
```

## 2. Is `(1 | Site_ID)` needed?

The null model with and without the site intercept. The ICC is the share of
the variance between sites. The likelihood-ratio test of a variance is on the
boundary (it can't be below 0), so the p-value is halved.

```{r ranef-check}
imap_dfr(RESPONSES, function(r, nm) {
  m_re <- lmer(reformulate("(1 | Site_ID)", response = r), data = dat, REML = FALSE)
  m_lm <- lm(reformulate("1", response = r), data = dat)
  vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m_re))$vcov
  lrt <- as.numeric(2 * (logLik(m_re) - logLik(m_lm)))
  tibble(response = RESP_LABELS[nm], sd_site = sqrt(vc[1]), sd_visit = sqrt(vc[2]),
         ICC = vc[1] / sum(vc), AIC_lm = AIC(m_lm), AIC_lmer = AIC(m_re),
         LRT = lrt, p = 0.5 * pchisq(lrt, df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE))
}) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Null model: site random intercept vs none")
```

## 3. Candidate pool and dredge

### 3.1 VIF screen and correlated pairs

Predictors are standardized over the 96 rows. `_dev` predictors are exactly
uncorrelated with all site-level predictors, so they pass the screen and are
never kept apart from them.

```{r vif}
int_mains <- unique(unlist(strsplit(INTERACTIONS, ":", fixed = TRUE)))
stopifnot(all(int_mains %in% all_preds))
protected <- unique(c(PROTECT, FIXED, int_mains))

vif_of <- function(X) {
  v <- tryCatch(diag(solve(cor(X))), error = function(e) rep(Inf, ncol(X)))
  setNames(v, colnames(X))
}

## Drop exact linear combinations, then the highest-VIF unprotected predictor
## until every VIF is below `thresh`
vif_stepdown <- function(X, thresh, protected) {
  log <- tibble(step = integer(), dropped = character(), vif = numeric())
  q <- qr(scale(X), tol = 1e-7)
  if (q$rank < ncol(X)) {
    aliased <- setdiff(colnames(X)[q$pivot[-seq_len(q$rank)]], protected)
    log <- add_row(log, step = seq_along(aliased), dropped = aliased, vif = Inf)
    X <- X[, setdiff(colnames(X), aliased), drop = FALSE]
  }
  repeat {
    v <- vif_of(X)
    cand <- v[setdiff(names(v), protected)]
    if (!is.finite(thresh) || length(cand) == 0 || max(v) < thresh || ncol(X) <= 2) break
    worst <- names(which.max(cand))
    log <- add_row(log, step = nrow(log) + 1L, dropped = worst, vif = max(cand))
    X <- X[, setdiff(colnames(X), worst), drop = FALSE]
  }
  list(dropped = log, vif = v)
}

vs <- vif_stepdown(as.matrix(dat[all_preds]), VIF_MAX, protected)
POOL <- names(vs$vif)

mdat <- dat |> mutate(across(all_of(POOL), \(v) as.numeric(scale(v))))

if (nrow(vs$dropped)) {
  print(kable(vs$dropped, digits = 2, caption = sprintf("Dropped by the VIF screen (VIF_MAX = %s)", VIF_MAX)))
}
tibble(predictor = POOL, level = pred_level(POOL), VIF = vs$vif,
       protected = POOL %in% protected) |>
  arrange(level, desc(VIF)) |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = sprintf("Candidate pool: %d predictors", length(POOL)))

rho <- cor(mdat[POOL], method = "spearman")
idx <- which(abs(rho) >= COR_MAX & upper.tri(rho), arr.ind = TRUE)
cor_pairs <- tibble(a = rownames(rho)[idx[, 1]], b = colnames(rho)[idx[, 2]], rho = rho[idx]) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(rho)))

## dredge subset matrix: FALSE = these two terms may not share a model.
## MuMIn reads only the lower triangle.
subset_mat <- abs(rho) < COR_MAX
subset_mat[!lower.tri(subset_mat)] <- NA

if (nrow(cor_pairs)) {
  kable(cor_pairs, digits = 2,
        caption = sprintf("Pairs with |ρ| ≥ %.2f: never in the same model", COR_MAX))
}
```

### 3.2 Dredge

```{r dredge-fns}
## Global model: all pool terms + interactions + the site intercept
global_formula <- function(resp) {
  reformulate(c(POOL, INTERACTIONS, "(1 | Site_ID)"), response = resp)
}

dredge_subset <- if (nrow(cor_pairs)) subset_mat

## Dredge one response on one data set. The formula, data and control are
## inlined into the lmer() call, so dredge and get.models() can re-fit any
## sub-model from any environment (CV fold, forked worker, later chunks).
run_dredge <- function(resp, d, evaluate = TRUE) {
  g <- suppressMessages(eval(bquote(lmer(.(global_formula(resp)), data = .(d), REML = FALSE,
                                         control = .(LMER_CTRL)))))
  suppressMessages(eval(bquote(
    dredge(g, rank = .(RANK), m.lim = c(M_MIN, M_MAX),
           fixed = .(if (length(FIXED)) FIXED else NULL),
           subset = .(dredge_subset), evaluate = .(evaluate))
  )))
}

## Parallel map (same approach as GHG_Dredge.qmd): fork where possible,
## otherwise a socket cluster; N_CORES = 1 runs serially.
CAN_FORK <- .Platform$OS.type == "unix" && tryCatch({
  mccollect(mcparallel(TRUE))
  TRUE
}, error = function(e) FALSE)

par_cl <- NULL

DREDGE_EXPORTS <- c("mdat", "run_dredge", "global_formula", "dredge_subset",
                    "POOL", "INTERACTIONS", "FIXED", "RANK", "M_MIN", "M_MAX",
                    "LMER_CTRL", "terms_in", "cand_terms", "null_gain")

par_map <- function(X, FUN, export = character()) {
  if (N_CORES <= 1) return(lapply(X, FUN))
  if (CAN_FORK) {
    out <- mclapply(X, FUN, mc.cores = N_CORES, mc.set.seed = TRUE)
    err <- keep(out, \(o) inherits(o, "try-error"))
    if (length(err)) stop("worker failed: ", err[[1]])
    return(out)
  }
  if (is.null(par_cl)) {
    par_cl <<- makeCluster(N_CORES)
    clusterEvalQ(par_cl, {
      suppressPackageStartupMessages({
        library(dplyr)
        library(purrr)
        library(lme4)
        library(MuMIn)
      })
      options(na.action = "na.fail")
    })
    clusterSetRNGStream(par_cl, SEED)
  }
  clusterExport(par_cl, export, envir = globalenv())
  parLapply(par_cl, X, FUN)
}

## Fixed terms dredge can switch on and off. nobars() drops (1 | Site_ID).
cand_terms <- setdiff(attr(terms(nobars(global_formula("CO2"))), "term.labels"), FIXED)

## Fixed terms in each row of a model.selection table
terms_in <- function(dd) {
  cols <- intersect(cand_terms, names(dd))
  apply(!is.na(as.data.frame(dd)[cols]), 1, \(r) cols[r], simplify = FALSE)
}

## Rank-criterion gain of the best model over the null (fixed terms only)
null_gain <- function(dd) {
  k <- lengths(terms_in(dd))
  if (!any(k == 0)) return(NA_real_)
  dd$delta[k == 0][1]
}

model_label <- function(tt) {
  fx <- if (length(FIXED)) sprintf("[%s]", paste(FIXED, collapse = " + ")) else character()
  map_chr(tt, \(t) {
    parts <- c(fx, t)
    if (length(parts)) paste(parts, collapse = " + ") else "(null)"
  })
}

## Marginal and conditional R2 of a merMod
r2_glmm <- function(m) {
  r2 <- suppressWarnings(r.squaredGLMM(m))
  c(R2m = unname(r2[1, "R2m"]), R2c = unname(r2[1, "R2c"]))
}

## Rough cost: models per dredge x seconds per fit
n_models <- length(run_dredge("CO2", mdat, evaluate = FALSE))
t_fit <- system.time(for (i in 1:20) suppressMessages(
  lmer(global_formula("CO2"), mdat, REML = FALSE, control = LMER_CTRL)))[["elapsed"]] / 20
n_folds <- switch(CV_SCHEME, site = 48, ecoregion = nlevels(dat$Ecoregion), none = 0, NA)
cat(sprintf(paste0(
  "%s parallel backend, %d cores\n",
  "%d models per dredge, ~%.0f ms per fit (global model) -> ~%.1f min per dredge\n",
  "Full run: %d dredges for 2 responses (1 + %d permutations + %s CV folds)\n"),
  if (N_CORES <= 1) "Serial" else if (CAN_FORK) "Forked" else "Socket-cluster", N_CORES,
  n_models, 1000 * t_fit, n_models * t_fit / 60,
  2 * (1 + N_PERM + ifelse(is.na(n_folds), 10, n_folds)), N_PERM,
  ifelse(is.na(n_folds), "~10", n_folds)))
```

```{r dredge-run}
dd_list <- map(RESPONSES, \(r) run_dredge(r, mdat))

tibble(response = RESP_LABELS[names(dd_list)],
       models_fitted = map_int(dd_list, nrow),
       top_set = map_int(dd_list, \(dd) sum(dd$delta < DELTA_TOP)),
       best_model = map_chr(dd_list, \(dd) model_label(terms_in(dd)[1])),
       best_weight = map_dbl(dd_list, \(dd) dd$weight[1]),
       null_rank = map_int(dd_list, \(dd) which(lengths(terms_in(dd)) == 0)[1]),
       null_delta = map_dbl(dd_list, null_gain)) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("Dredge summary (%s, at most %d fixed terms)", RANK, M_MAX))
```

### 3.3 Top model sets

`sd_site` is the site random-intercept SD left after the fixed effects. If
site-level predictors explain site differences, it shrinks relative to the
null model in Section 2. `singular` = the site variance was estimated at 0.

```{r top-sets, results = "asis"}
for (nm in names(dd_list)) {
  dd <- dd_list[[nm]]
  top <- dd[dd$delta < DELTA_TOP, ]
  fits <- get.models(top, subset = TRUE)
  r2 <- map(fits, r2_glmm)
  tibble(model = model_label(terms_in(top)), df = top$df,
         R2m = map_dbl(r2, "R2m"), R2c = map_dbl(r2, "R2c"),
         sd_site = map_dbl(fits, sd_site),
         singular = map_lgl(fits, isSingular),
         !!RANK := top[[RANK]], delta = top$delta, weight = top$weight) |>
    kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("%s: top set (delta < %g)", RESP_LABELS[nm], DELTA_TOP)) |>
    print()
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

### 3.4 Predictor importance (summed weights)

Summed Akaike weight over all models containing each predictor. Green bars
are visit-level (within-site) predictors. The tick is the expected sum if
every model had equal weight.

```{r importance, fig.height=6}
imp <- imap_dfr(dd_list, function(dd, nm) {
  tt <- terms_in(dd)
  tibble(response = nm, term = cand_terms, level = pred_level(cand_terms),
         sw = map_dbl(cand_terms, \(t) sum(dd$weight[map_lgl(tt, \(x) t %in% x)])),
         equal_w = map_dbl(cand_terms, \(t) mean(map_lgl(tt, \(x) t %in% x))))
})

imp_order <- imp |> group_by(term) |> summarise(m = max(sw)) |> arrange(m) |> pull(term)

ggplot(imp, aes(sw, factor(term, levels = imp_order))) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = level), width = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(x = equal_w), shape = 124, size = 4, color = "#3a3936") +
  facet_wrap(~response, labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = LEVEL_COLS) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(title = "Summed model weight per predictor",
       subtitle = "Tick = expected sum if all models were equally supported",
       x = "Summed weight", y = NULL, fill = "Predictor level")
```

### 3.5 Coefficients: top model and model average

Full model average over the top set (absent terms count as 0). Wald 95%
intervals, not adjusted for the selection step.

```{r coefs, fig.height=6}
coef_df <- imap_dfr(dd_list, function(dd, nm) {
  best <- get.models(dd, 1)[[1]]
  ci <- confint(best, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")
  out <- tibble(response = nm, model = "top model", term = names(fixef(best)),
                estimate = unname(fixef(best)), lo = ci[, 1], hi = ci[, 2])
  if (sum(dd$delta < DELTA_TOP) > 1) {
    av <- model.avg(dd, subset = delta < DELTA_TOP)
    cf <- coef(av, full = TRUE)
    ci <- confint(av, full = TRUE)
    out <- bind_rows(out, tibble(response = nm, model = "top-set average", term = names(cf),
                                 estimate = unname(cf), lo = ci[names(cf), 1], hi = ci[names(cf), 2]))
  }
  out
}) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)")

if (nrow(coef_df)) {
  ggplot(coef_df, aes(estimate, term, color = model)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "#c3c2b7") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0,
                   position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.4, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
    facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free_x", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`top model` = "#2a78d6", `top-set average` = "#898781")) +
    labs(title = "Coefficients per 1 SD of each predictor",
         subtitle = "95% Wald intervals, not adjusted for model selection",
         x = "Estimate", y = NULL, color = NULL)
} else {
  cat("Both top models are the null model: no coefficients to show.\n")
}
```

### 3.6 Top-model diagnostics

Visit-level residuals (after the site intercept) and the site intercepts
themselves. Both should look roughly normal.

```{r diag, fig.height=7}
top_fits <- map(dd_list, \(dd) get.models(dd, 1)[[1]])

diag_d <- imap_dfr(top_fits, \(m, nm) tibble(
  response = nm, fitted = fitted(m), resid = residuals(m), Wetland_Type = mdat$Wetland_Type))
re_d <- imap_dfr(top_fits, \(m, nm) tibble(response = nm, ranef = ranef(m)$Site_ID[, 1]))

rf <- ggplot(diag_d, aes(fitted, resid)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_point(aes(color = Wetland_Type, shape = Wetland_Type), size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = WT_COLS) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = WT_SHAPES) +
  labs(title = "Top model: visit residuals vs fitted", x = "Fitted", y = "Residual",
       color = "Wetland type", shape = "Wetland type")

qq_resid <- ggplot(diag_d, aes(sample = resid)) +
  stat_qq_line(color = "#c3c2b7") +
  stat_qq(size = 1.6, color = "#2a78d6") +
  facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
  labs(title = "Visit residuals: normal Q-Q", x = "Theoretical", y = "Sample")

qq_re <- ggplot(re_d, aes(sample = ranef)) +
  stat_qq_line(color = "#c3c2b7") +
  stat_qq(size = 1.6, color = "#898781") +
  facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
  labs(title = "Site intercepts: normal Q-Q", x = "Theoretical", y = "Sample")

rf / (qq_resid | qq_re)
```

## 4. Is the selected model better than chance?

### 4.1 Restricted permutation test

Each shuffle moves the response of whole sites (both visits together) to
other sites, then swaps the two visits within each site with probability
0.5. This keeps the site variance (the null model is unchanged) and breaks
the link to both site-level and visit-level predictors. Dredge is re-run
with the same settings. p = share of shuffles whose best model beats the
null by at least as much as the real data's.

```{r perm}
## Rows are ordered site by site, rounds 1 and 2 adjacent (checked in Section 1)
shuffle_paired <- function(y) {
  Y <- matrix(y, nrow = 2)                 # column = site, rows = rounds
  Y <- Y[, sample(ncol(Y)), drop = FALSE]  # move whole sites
  flip <- runif(ncol(Y)) < 0.5             # swap visits within sites
  Y[, flip] <- Y[2:1, flip]
  as.vector(Y)
}

perm_res <- if (N_PERM > 0) {
  imap(RESPONSES, function(r, nm) {
    obs <- null_gain(dd_list[[nm]])
    perm <- unlist(par_map(seq_len(N_PERM), function(i) {
      d <- mdat
      d[[r]] <- shuffle_paired(d[[r]])
      null_gain(run_dredge(r, d))
    }, export = c(DREDGE_EXPORTS, "shuffle_paired")))
    list(obs = obs, perm = perm, p = (sum(perm >= obs) + 1) / (N_PERM + 1))
  })
}
```

```{r perm-plot, fig.height=4}
if (N_PERM > 0) {
  perm_long <- imap_dfr(perm_res, \(p, nm) tibble(response = nm, gain = p$perm))
  perm_obs <- imap_dfr(perm_res, \(p, nm) tibble(
    response = nm, gain = p$obs, lab = sprintf("observed = %.1f\np = %.3f", p$obs, p$p)))

  print(
    ggplot(perm_long, aes(gain)) +
      geom_histogram(aes(fill = response), bins = 25, color = "white", show.legend = FALSE) +
      geom_vline(data = perm_obs, aes(xintercept = gain), color = "#3a3936", linewidth = 0.8) +
      geom_text(data = perm_obs, aes(x = gain, y = Inf, label = lab),
                hjust = -0.08, vjust = 1.3, size = 3.3, color = "#3a3936") +
      facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = RESP_COLS) +
      labs(title = sprintf("Best-model gain over the null: real data vs %d shuffles", N_PERM),
           x = sprintf("Null model delta %s", RANK), y = "Shuffles")
  )
}
```

### 4.2 Nested cross-validation (new sites)

In each fold, dredge is re-run on the training sites, and the selected
model's fixed effects predict both visits of the held-out sites
(`re.form = NA`). Baseline = training mean. **Predictive R² ≤ 0 means no
better than that mean.** Visit-level predictors still help here if
within-site weather matters, because the held-out visits' weather is known.

```{r cv-folds}
site_xy <- mdat |> distinct(Site_ID, x, y, Ecoregion)
site_fold <- switch(CV_SCHEME,
  site = seq_len(nrow(site_xy)),
  spatial = cutree(hclust(dist(site_xy[c("x", "y")]) / 1000, method = "complete"), h = CV_BLOCK_KM),
  ecoregion = as.integer(site_xy$Ecoregion),
  none = NULL
)
cv_folds <- if (!is.null(site_fold)) site_fold[match(mdat$Site_ID, site_xy$Site_ID)]
if (!is.null(cv_folds)) {
  cat(sprintf("%d folds; held-out sites per fold: min %d, median %g, max %d\n",
              n_distinct(site_fold), min(table(site_fold)), median(table(site_fold)),
              max(table(site_fold))))
}
```

```{r cv}
predict_fold <- function(dd, newdata) {
  if (CV_PREDICT == "average" && sum(dd$delta < DELTA_TOP) > 1) {
    predict(model.avg(get.models(dd, subset = delta < DELTA_TOP)), newdata = newdata,
            full = TRUE, re.form = NA)
  } else {
    predict(get.models(dd, 1)[[1]], newdata = newdata, re.form = NA)
  }
}

cv_res <- if (!is.null(cv_folds)) {
  imap(RESPONSES, function(r, nm) {
    folds <- par_map(sort(unique(cv_folds)), function(k) {
      test <- cv_folds == k
      dd <- run_dredge(r, droplevels(mdat[!test, ]))
      list(pred = tibble(row = which(test), pred = unname(predict_fold(dd, mdat[test, ])),
                         base = mean(mdat[[r]][!test])),
           terms = terms_in(dd)[[1]])
    }, export = c(DREDGE_EXPORTS, "cv_folds", "predict_fold", "CV_PREDICT", "DELTA_TOP"))
    pred <- map_dfr(folds, "pred") |>
      arrange(row) |>
      mutate(obs = mdat[[r]][row], Site_ID = mdat$Site_ID[row],
             Wetland_Type = mdat$Wetland_Type[row])
    list(pred = pred, terms = map(folds, "terms"))
  })
}
```

Two scores: per visit, and per site (mean of the two visits' observed and
predicted values, comparable to `GHG_Dredge.qmd`).

```{r cv-table}
pred_r2 <- function(obs, pred, base) 1 - sum((obs - pred)^2) / sum((obs - base)^2)

if (!is.null(cv_folds)) {
  imap_dfr(cv_res, function(cv, nm) {
    site <- cv$pred |> group_by(Site_ID) |> summarise(across(c(obs, pred, base), mean))
    r2 <- r2_glmm(get.models(dd_list[[nm]], 1)[[1]])
    tibble(response = RESP_LABELS[nm],
           RMSE_selected = with(cv$pred, sqrt(mean((obs - pred)^2))),
           RMSE_mean = with(cv$pred, sqrt(mean((obs - base)^2))),
           cv_R2_visit = with(cv$pred, pred_r2(obs, pred, base)),
           cv_R2_site = with(site, pred_r2(obs, pred, base)),
           in_sample_R2m = r2[["R2m"]], in_sample_R2c = r2[["R2c"]])
  }) |>
    kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("Nested CV (%s folds, %s prediction, fixed effects only)",
                                        CV_SCHEME, CV_PREDICT))
}
```

```{r cv-plot, fig.height=4.5}
if (!is.null(cv_folds)) {
  cvp <- imap_dfr(cv_res, \(cv, nm) mutate(cv$pred, response = nm))
  ggplot(cvp, aes(obs, pred)) +
    geom_abline(color = "#c3c2b7") +
    geom_line(aes(group = Site_ID), color = "#e1e0d9") +
    geom_point(aes(color = Wetland_Type, shape = Wetland_Type), size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = WT_COLS) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = WT_SHAPES) +
    labs(title = "Held-out predictions from the nested CV",
         subtitle = "Solid = 1:1; grey segments join a site's two visits",
         x = "Observed", y = "Predicted (held out, fixed effects only)",
         color = "Wetland type", shape = "Wetland type")
}
```

### 4.3 Selection stability across folds

```{r stability, fig.height=5}
if (!is.null(cv_folds)) {
  stab <- imap_dfr(cv_res, function(cv, nm) {
    tibble(response = nm, term = cand_terms, level = pred_level(cand_terms),
           freq = map_dbl(cand_terms, \(t) mean(map_lgl(cv$terms, \(x) t %in% x))))
  }) |>
    group_by(term) |> filter(max(freq) > 0) |> ungroup()

  stab_order <- stab |> group_by(term) |> summarise(m = max(freq)) |> arrange(m) |> pull(term)

  print(
    ggplot(stab, aes(freq, factor(term, levels = stab_order))) +
      geom_col(aes(fill = level), width = 0.7) +
      facet_wrap(~response, labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = LEVEL_COLS) +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
      labs(title = "Share of CV folds whose best model includes each predictor",
           subtitle = "Predictors never selected are omitted", x = NULL, y = NULL,
           fill = "Predictor level")
  )

  imap_dfr(cv_res, \(cv, nm) tibble(response = RESP_LABELS[nm], model = model_label(cv$terms))) |>
    count(response, model, sort = TRUE) |>
    group_by(response) |> slice_head(n = 5) |> ungroup() |>
    kable(caption = "Most common best models across CV folds (top 5 per response)")
}
```

### 4.4 Summary

```{r summary}
tibble(
  response = RESP_LABELS[names(dd_list)],
  best_model = map_chr(dd_list, \(dd) model_label(terms_in(dd)[1])),
  R2m = map_dbl(top_fits, \(m) r2_glmm(m)[["R2m"]]),
  gain_over_null = map_dbl(dd_list, null_gain),
  perm_p = if (N_PERM > 0) map_dbl(perm_res, "p") else NA_real_,
  cv_R2_site = if (!is.null(cv_folds)) {
    map_dbl(cv_res, \(cv) {
      s <- cv$pred |> group_by(Site_ID) |> summarise(across(c(obs, pred, base), mean))
      pred_r2(s$obs, s$pred, s$base)
    })
  } else NA_real_
) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Does the dredge selection hold up?")
```

## 5. Candidate formulas

Hand-picked fixed effects from `CANDIDATES`, each fitted with
`(1 | Site_ID)` and compared with the null model, its own fixed effects
without interactions, and dredge's best model. Same caveat as in
`GHG_Dredge.qmd`: in-sample numbers and the CV assume the formula was chosen
before seeing the data.

```{r cand, results = "asis"}
if (length(CANDIDATES)) {
cdat <- dat |> mutate(across(all_of(all_preds), \(v) as.numeric(scale(v))))
cand_resp <- function(f) all.vars(f[[2]])
cand_vars <- function(f) all.vars(f[[3]])
resp_name <- function(f) names(RESPONSES)[RESPONSES == cand_resp(f)]
add_re <- function(f) update(f, . ~ . + (1 | Site_ID))
## Formula and data inlined into the call, so drop1() can refit it
fit_re <- function(f, d = cdat) {
  suppressMessages(eval(bquote(lmer(.(add_re(f)), data = .(d), REML = FALSE,
                                    control = .(LMER_CTRL)))))
}

walk(CANDIDATES, function(f) {
  stopifnot(cand_resp(f) %in% RESPONSES)
  bad <- setdiff(cand_vars(f), names(cdat))
  if (length(bad)) stop("unknown predictor(s): ", paste(bad, collapse = ", "))
})

cdat_site <- cdat |> distinct(Site_ID, x, y, Ecoregion)
cand_folds <- list(
  site = as.integer(cdat$Site_ID),
  spatial = cutree(hclust(dist(cdat_site[c("x", "y")]) / 1000, method = "complete"),
                   h = CV_BLOCK_KM)[match(cdat$Site_ID, cdat_site$Site_ID)],
  ecoregion = as.integer(cdat$Ecoregion)
)
cv_fixed <- function(f, folds) {
  y <- cdat[[cand_resp(f)]]
  pred <- base <- numeric(length(y))
  for (k in unique(folds)) {
    test <- folds == k
    pred[test] <- predict(fit_re(f, droplevels(cdat[!test, ])), newdata = cdat[test, ], re.form = NA)
    base[test] <- mean(y[!test])
  }
  pred_r2(y, pred, base)
}

iwalk(CANDIDATES, function(f, nm) {
  r <- cand_resp(f)
  comp <- list(
    `null` = reformulate("1", response = r),
    `main effects only` = reformulate(cand_vars(f), response = r),
    `dredge best` = nobars(formula(get.models(dd_list[[resp_name(f)]], 1)[[1]])),
    candidate = f
  )
  comp <- comp[!duplicated(map_chr(comp, \(x) paste(deparse(x), collapse = "")))]
  imap_dfr(comp, function(fc, lab) {
    m <- fit_re(fc)
    r2 <- r2_glmm(m)
    tibble(model = lab, formula = paste(deparse(fc[[3]], width.cutoff = 500), collapse = ""),
           k = length(fixef(m)), R2m = r2[["R2m"]], R2c = r2[["R2c"]], AICc = AICc(m),
           sd_site = sd_site(m),
           cv_site = cv_fixed(fc, cand_folds$site),
           cv_spatial = cv_fixed(fc, cand_folds$spatial),
           cv_ecoregion = cv_fixed(fc, cand_folds$ecoregion))
  }) |>
    kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("%s (%s): comparison (cv_* = visit-level predictive R²)",
                                        nm, RESP_LABELS[resp_name(f)])) |>
    print()
  cat("\n\n")

  m <- fit_re(f)
  d1 <- drop1(m, test = "Chisq")
  tibble(term = rownames(d1)[-1], LRT = d1$LRT[-1], p = d1$`Pr(Chi)`[-1]) |>
    kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("%s: likelihood-ratio tests of the highest-order terms", nm)) |>
    print()
  cat("\n\n")
  cf <- summary(m)$coefficients
  tibble(term = rownames(cf), estimate = cf[, 1], SE = cf[, 2], t = cf[, 3]) |>
    kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("%s: fixed effects (per 1 SD)", nm)) |>
    print()
  cat("\n\n")
})}
```

## 6. Typical-summer-day prediction

Predictions at each site with `<v>_dev = 0` and `<v>_site` at the reference
value (`REF_WEATHER`, default the median of the site means), from the top
model's fixed effects (`re.form = NA`, as for an unsampled location). Site-level
predictors keep their observed values. On the model scale; for log-shifted
CH4, `exp(prediction) - c` is a median, not a mean, flux.

```{r upscale, fig.height=4}
if (WEATHER_SPLIT) {
  site_vars <- paste0(visit_short, "_site")
  ref <- map_dbl(set_names(site_vars), \(v) {
    if (v %in% names(REF_WEATHER)) REF_WEATHER[[v]] else median(dat[[v]][c(TRUE, FALSE)])
  })
  print(kable(tibble(variable = names(ref), reference_raw = ref), digits = 2,
              caption = "Reference weather (raw units)"))

  ## Reference data on the standardized scale of mdat
  ref_dat <- dat[c(TRUE, FALSE), ]
  for (v in site_vars) ref_dat[[v]] <- ref[[v]]
  for (v in paste0(visit_short, "_dev")) ref_dat[[v]] <- 0
  for (v in intersect(POOL, names(ref_dat))) {
    ref_dat[[v]] <- (ref_dat[[v]] - mean(dat[[v]])) / sd(dat[[v]])
  }

  up <- imap_dfr(top_fits, \(m, nm) tibble(
    response = nm, Site_ID = ref_dat$Site_ID, Wetland_Type = ref_dat$Wetland_Type,
    typical = unname(predict(m, newdata = ref_dat, re.form = NA)),
    observed_site_mean = tapply(mdat[[RESPONSES[[nm]]]], mdat$Site_ID, mean)[as.character(ref_dat$Site_ID)]))

  ggplot(up, aes(observed_site_mean, typical)) +
    geom_abline(color = "#c3c2b7") +
    geom_point(aes(color = Wetland_Type, shape = Wetland_Type), size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = WT_COLS) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = WT_SHAPES) +
    labs(title = "Top model at reference weather vs observed site mean",
         x = "Observed site mean (model scale)", y = "Predicted, typical summer day",
         color = "Wetland type", shape = "Wetland type")
}
```
